skill.name: google-calendar-automation

static_findings.snippet: All operations via `scripts/gcal.py`. Auto-authenticates on first use if not logged in.
- Primary calendar: Use `primary` or omit the `--calendar` flag
- Other calendars: Use the calendar ID from `list-calendars` (usually an email address)

content.value_statement: Manual schedule updates slow teams down and create missed meetings. This skill guides OAuth-backed Google Calendar listing, event management, RSVP handling, and free-time checks.
actual_capabilities: Lists Google Calendar calendars through the documented local command workflow.
Lists events from a primary or selected calendar within a time range.
Creates events with title, time, description, location, calendar, and attendees.
Updates event title, time, description, location, and attendee fields.
Deletes events and responds to invitations as accepted, declined, or tentative.
Searches for available meeting slots across specified attendees and time windows.
limitations: Requires a Google Workspace account; personal Gmail accounts are not supported.
Requires OAuth authentication and the necessary Google Calendar permissions.
The scanned package documents scripts but does not include their executable source.
Date and time inputs must use ISO 8601 format with a timezone.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Team Meetings
use_cases.description: Find open slots, create meetings, and invite attendees without opening the calendar interface.

use_cases.title: Maintain Operational Calendars
use_cases.description: List upcoming events, update details, and delete outdated entries for shared work calendars.

use_cases.title: Handle Calendar Invitations
use_cases.description: Inspect invitations and respond with accepted, declined, or tentative status from a local workflow.

prompt_templates.title: List My Calendars
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Google Calendar skill to check authentication, then list every calendar available to my Workspace account.

prompt_templates.title: Review Upcoming Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my primary calendar events for the next two weeks. Include event title, start time, end time, and calendar name.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Meeting
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 45 minute project review next Tuesday at 2 PM with two attendees, a short agenda, and the main office location.

prompt_templates.title: Find and Book Free Time
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the first 60 minute slot this week between 9 AM and 5 PM for three attendees, then create the meeting after I confirm.

output_examples.input: List available calendars for my Workspace account.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports the primary calendar and any shared work calendars, including each visible calendar name and identifier.

output_examples.input: Find a one hour slot for me and two coworkers this week.
output_examples.output: The assistant returns the earliest matching time window and explains which attendees were checked.

output_examples.input: Move an existing meeting and update the agenda.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the event identifier, new time, updated description, and whether attendees should be notified.

best_practices: Confirm the target calendar before creating, updating, or deleting events.
Use explicit timezone offsets in every date and time request.
Review attendee lists before sending invitations or responses.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill with personal Gmail accounts.
Do not delete or update events without checking the event identifier first.
Do not assume free-time results are final when attendees use external calendars.

faq.question: Does this skill work with personal Gmail?
faq.answer: No. The documentation says a Google Workspace account is required.

faq.question: Does it need an MCP server?
faq.answer: No. It is designed around standalone OAuth authentication and local script commands.

faq.question: What can it do with events?
faq.answer: It can list, inspect, create, update, delete, and respond to Google Calendar events.

faq.question: Can it find free time for several people?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow checks attendees within a chosen time window and duration.

faq.question: Where are OAuth tokens stored?
faq.answer: The documentation says tokens are stored in the system keyring, such as Keychain or Credential Locker.

faq.question: What should I verify before use?
faq.answer: Verify the included scripts, OAuth permissions, calendar identifiers, and timezone values in your environment.
